text:
oncall-bot: ALERT -> tenant=bluewave-llc | pool=dedicated-pool-us-west-2-b | symptom=quality_regression_longform | metrics=[cust_eval_bleu:-22%, hallucination_rate:+9%] | possible_cause=quant_profile_rollout | severity=P2. Paging @jordan (oncall). Start tenant-scoped coordination thread.

jordan: on it. pulling tenant evals and runtime traces. thanks for the page.

ryan: I'm standing by for rollback. Which profile did we push?

jordan: model shows rdx-6b-quant-alpha deployed to tenant at 2089950000 as part of a fleet update. Canary was small but alpha ramped for the dedicated shard overnight. Non-tenant baselines look fine.

natalie: CS note: BlueWave reported a few production mismatches in morning QA to their ops contact; they flagged examples but didn't attach logs. They're running a VPC-dedicated deployment with strict SLA.

jordan: hypothesis: quant-alpha reduces fp-range leading to degraded fluency on long-context templates specific to BlueWave's prompts. Tenant-specific eval BLEU dropped ~22%, unacceptably high.

research-bot: quick eval summary -> tenant_prompt_set_2026-03-14: BLEU -22%, ROUGE-L -7%, perplexity +15%. Control group (other tenants) within expected variance.

ryan: two mitigation options: A) immediate tenant rollback to rdx-6b-quant-stable (fast), B) route tenant to rdx-6b-fp16-hosted (different quant scheme) while we debug, C) apply on-the-fly postprocessing to filter hallucinations. I vote rollback.

jordan: agree. rollback path: create a 10% canary route then 100% flip if canary passes. I'll run commands and watch.

devops-bot: creating incident ticket INC-2089997 and tagging eng-ml, oncall. Incident owner alias: jordan.

jordan: running canary now. commands:
```
# create canary route for BlueWave
rctl routes create --tenant bluewave-llc --pool dedicated-pool-us-west-2-b --route canary-quant-stable --target-model rdx-6b-quant-stable --traffic 10
# stream canary logs
rctl logs tail --route canary-quant-stable --since 2m
```

(3m)

jordan: canary sample looks much better: BLEU delta now -3% vs tenant baseline. hallucination_rate down to +1. Latency unchanged.

ryan: good. proceed to shift 100% traffic.

jordan: executing full flip:
```
rctl routes update --tenant bluewave-llc --route default --target-model rdx-6b-quant-stable
```

(4m)

jordan: rollout complete. post-rollback checks: tenant_eval BLEU back to baseline (+2%), hallucination within +0-2%, no surge in errors. controller reports success at 2089998037.

devops-bot: Mitigation recorded: rolled BlueWave from rdx-6b-quant-alpha -> rdx-6b-quant-stable at 2089998037. Linked INC-2089997.

natalie: sending customer-facing note to BlueWave ops lead: "We've identified a model quantization change impacting long-form outputs for your tenant; we've reverted the profile and metrics are back to expected levels. We'll follow up with details and a scheduled postmortem." Will attach the examples they sent.

jordan: immediate next actions:
- open postmortem draft (owner: ryan) due in 72h
- add tenant-scoped gating to quant profile rollout checklist (owner: eng-ml)
- add automated pre-rollout evals for any tenant with dedicated pools/VPC (owner: research)
- implement short-term alert: per-tenant BLEU drop >10% in 30m triggers page (owner: observability)

ryan: adding a runbook note: for dedicated-tenant rollouts, require a 10% tenant canary for 30m with automated eval comparisons before 100% ramp.

jordan: handing off to night oncall @jordan_night in 30m. leaving rollback commands and incident links in INC-2089997. If anything regresses, page oncall->sev1 escalation.

natalie: BlueWave replied: appreciate the fast fix. Requested a brief sync next week to review internal test cases. Scheduling.

research-bot: logging dataset artifacts: tenant_prompt_set_2026-03-14.zip attached to the ticket for offline analysis.

jordan: closing thread here—will paste postmortem link when ryan publishes. :white_check_mark:
